name: Heavy metal football (merged with the Red Bull school)
scopeNote: MERGED PROFILE (user decision, 2026-11-03): the Red Bull school (Rangnick, Nagelsmann, Marsch; former red-bull-school.json, kept on disk) is merged into heavy metal football; gegenpressing and vertical-football stay separate profiles. Both groups use the term: Klopp coined 'heavy metal' (Nov 2013) and Rangnick says 'Our Red Bull football is heavy metal, rock and roll' (planetfootball, 2021, attributed). Exemplar group 1: Klopp's Liverpool 2018/19-2019/20 (and the Klopp quote from Dortmund-Arsenal, Nov 2013). Exemplar group 2: the Red Bull pressing-and-vertical school from Rangnick's arrival at Salzburg/Leipzig in 2012 (partial date, exact day not found) through Nagelsmann at Leipzig 2019-21 and Marsch at Salzburg 2019-21; Sources 'group' field marks klopp-liverpool vs red-bull. profilePeriod is 2012 to ongoing because the earliest fact is the Red Bull 2012 recruitment policy; Klopp-side facts date 2013-2020. The groups differ: Liverpool 4-3-3 with ~60% possession and high full-backs; Red Bull pressing traps with a man-oriented back line (Rangnick/Schmidt, Marsch), trigger-based zonal press (Hasenhuttl) or 5-2-3 trap out wide (Nagelsmann). Popular labels to watch: 'gegenpressing' is incomplete for Red Bull (Spielverlagerung: pressing trap system with fast vertical attack); 'counter-attacking only' is wrong for Liverpool (Coaches' Voice ~60% possession); Sportskeeda 2019 says Liverpool pressed less than in 2017/18 while Premier League.com 2020 says the press reverted to frenetic in 2019/20; Klopp tried to shed the phrase in Nov 2015. Marking: Leipzig set-pieces are mixed zonal (five zonal markers) plus man-markers (TFA 2019/20); Leipzig/Marsch open-play press is man-oriented; Liverpool's open-play pressing marking has no verified source (one search found none). Nagelsmann 70/30 quote undated; Coaches Voice article date 2024-06-28 used. Bleacher Report metadata date (2018) is wrong; interview autumn 2013.
openQuestions: Exemplar team id: no Liverpool 2018-20 team file exists in profile-audit/research/team (only liverpool-1976-84 and liverpool-2021-22); proposed id liverpool-2018-20 with manager jurgen-klopp (2018-07-01 to 2020-07-26 approx.). Manager id jurgen-klopp exists. Not created here.

Origin of the quote: Goal.com says Klopp told the Daily Mail; Bleacher Report carries the same words with no outlet named and a wrong metadata date. No primary Daily Mail page was read; exact date (Nov 2013) is not confirmed. One web summary says Demba Ba told of a Klopp-Rangnick origin story (FourFourTwo) - not read, unverified.

Is Liverpool 2018-20 really 'heavy metal'? Sportskeeda 2019 and Coaches' Voice show a more controlled, possession-heavy, full-back-driven side; Premier League.com shows press intensity back up in 2019/20 (largest rise in final-third turnovers). Pressing-intensity data conflict between This Is Anfield/Tifo PPDA claims (seen only in search summaries, pages 403) and Premier League.com. A later profile may prefer Dortmund 2010-13 or Liverpool 2016-18 as purer exemplars.
Marking: Liverpool's zonal set-piece defending per Lucas Leiva and a part-zonal part-man mix per Tomkins Times were seen only in search summaries (pages 404 or not accessible), so unverified.

Squad building and people management evidence is thin: Alisson (2020) on equal treatment and a Klopp-recalled half-time row (retrospective); signings (Van Dijk, Alisson, Fabinho, Keita) seen only in search summaries.
Proposed ids: ralf-rangnick exists in manager catalog; julian-nagelsmann and jesse-marsch not found in profile-audit/research/manager, proposed ids julian-nagelsmann and jesse-marsch.
Rangnick's own Red Bull-era tactical coverage is mostly via Spielverlagerung 2017 (Leipzig 2015/16) and quotes; no primary tier A study of Salzburg 2012-15 found.

Marking: Spielverlagerung says Rangnick's Leipzig back line marked strikers and Breaking the Lines says Marsch's Salzburg is man-oriented, but a search summary (unverified) called Salzburg ball-oriented; The Master Minds pages were 403.
Marsch's New York Red Bulls (2015-18) and Hasenhuttl/Schmidt as exemplars not researched; Nagelsmann's quotes undated in Coaches' Voice.
Spielverlagerung article says Hasenhuttl's Leipzig is 'in contrary to the public opinion' not full-force in first pressing phase, which contradicts the popular total-press image.

Name of the merged ideology: 'heavy metal football' is Klopp's coinage and also Rangnick's self-description, but 'Red Bull school' and 'Rangnick school' are the common names for the second group and Klopp tried to drop the phrase in 2015. Should the merged profile keep 'heavy metal football', or be renamed (e.g. 'heavy metal / Red Bull school')? Overlap with gegenpressing and vertical-football remains to be policed in exemplars.

statedView.quote: He likes having the ball, playing football, passes... it’s like an orchestra ... but it is a silent song. I like heavy metal more. I always want it loud.
statedView.source: Klopp on Wenger's Arsenal before Dortmund v Arsenal, Champions League; Bleacher Report (https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1836331-jurgen-klopp-gives-fascinating-view-on-arsene-wenger-before-dortmund-vs-arsenal); Goal.com attributes it to the Daily Mail but no Daily Mail page was read

statedView.quote: I don’t like winning with 80 per cent (of possession). Sorry that is not enough for me. Fighting football, not serenity football, that is what I like.
statedView.source: same interview as above, Bleacher Report

statedView.quote: The problem with my life is I have said too many s*** words in the past! And no one forgets it
statedView.source: Klopp on being asked about heavy metal at Liverpool, FourFourTwo (https://fourfourtwo.com/news/klopp-keen-change-heavy-metal-record); Trivela adds 'maybe create a new kind of music'

statedView.quote: Our Red Bull football is heavy metal, rock and roll, it's not a slow waltz. We hate square passes, back passes, just having the ball ourselves doesn't make sense.
statedView.speaker: Ralf Rangnick

statedView.quote: We like to press high, with a very intense counter-pressure. When we have the ball, we do not like any square or back passes.
statedView.speaker: Ralf Rangnick

statedView.quote: Thirty per cent of coaching is tactics, 70 per cent social competence
statedView.speaker: Julian Nagelsmann

statedView.quote: Der Fußball damals, mit dem überfallartigen Pressing, im Moment des Ballgewinns mit sechs sieben Spieler in den gegnerischen Strafraum zu sprinten.
statedView.speaker: Julian Nagelsmann

statedView.quote: I have even often said to our scouting department maybe the best way of thinking about how to scout players is to think about what leagues and clubs around the world play a similar brand of football to what we do.
statedView.speaker: Jesse Marsch

statedView.quote: there's a contagiousness to the feeling of overwhelming the opponent by outrunning them, by pressing them, by giving them no time on the ball
statedView.speaker: Jesse Marsch

exemplars.reason: Coined the label (2013) and ran the style at Dortmund and Liverpool; counted spell Liverpool 2015-10-08 to 2024-05-31.
Task 5 exemplar: 4-3-3 with Salah/Mane/Firmino, attacking full-backs, press back to high intensity in 2019/20 (Premier League.com). Team file not yet created; id proposed.
Founder: Leipzig 2015/16 and sporting director at Salzburg and Leipzig
Rangnick-schooled; Leipzig 2019-21 trap press out wide, more possession
Salzburg 2019-21 man-oriented 2v1 press, self-declared admirer of Rangnick

influences: Gegenpressing / counter-pressing (Rangnick, Wolfgang Frank at Mainz) - see gegenpressing.json
English football ('fighting football, not serenity football', rainy day, heavy pitch, 5-5; Bleacher Report 2013)
Manchester United's high-tempo style of the 2000s (Bleacher Report, journalist's comparison)
Valeriy Lobanovskyi's Dynamo Kyiv (via Rangnick, unverified)

confidence.reason: Red Bull side has several tier A-B sources (Coaches' Voice, StatsBomb, Spielverlagerung, Breaking the Lines, TFA) that agree on pressing traps and vertical attack; Liverpool side rests on one Coaches' Voice page plus tier B/C sources that partly disagree on how 'heavy metal' it was; Liverpool open-play marking and Rangnick-era Salzburg are thin; the merge joins two different styles under one label.
